title: Output confirmations — drive what the provider echoes back, matching and mismatched
description: The drive half of an output contract. After the IoBlock's [Timer(1)] has commanded its digital and analog outputs, serviceProviderSet drives the confirmation a service provider would send back on those same contracts — the DigitalOutputChanged / AnalogOutputChanged inbound — and the block's OutputChanged handlers surface it. First a truthful confirmation (the block sees no mismatch), then a deliberately WRONG one: the provider reports false on an output commanded true, which no real hardware would produce on demand, and the block's mismatch flag rises. Everything runs stepped, so the whole loop is deterministic.

steps.label: wait until the block observes the digital input
fire the [Timer(1)] so the block commands both outputs
the digital output was commanded true
the provider confirms the digital output as commanded
wait until the block observes the confirmation
a truthful confirmation raises no mismatch
the provider confirms the analog output as commanded
wait until the analog confirmation arrives
the provider now confirms FALSE on an output commanded true
wait until the block notices the disagreement
the block reports what the provider said, not what it asked for
commanded true, confirmed false — the mismatch is visible
